stem: In each of the following two-digit numbers, the product of the two digits follows a pattern in three of them. Which number does NOT fit the pattern? 34, 43, 62, 39

per_option_rationale.rationale: 34: 3 x 4 = 12. The digit product is 12, fitting the pattern. A student may focus on the digit sum (3+4=7) instead of the digit product.
43: 4 x 3 = 12. The digit product is 12, same as 34. Both 34 and 43 are digit-reversal pairs, so a student might flag 43 as a duplicate of 34, but duplicates are allowed in the pattern group.
62: 6 x 2 = 12. The digit product is 12, fitting the pattern. A student misapplying the pattern as digit sum might compute 6+2=8 and incorrectly flag 62.
39: 3 x 9 = 27, not 12. The other three (34, 43, 62) all have a digit product of 12. 39 has a digit product of 27, breaking the pattern.

explanation: The common property: digit product = 12. 34: 3x4=12; 43: 4x3=12; 62: 6x2=12; 39: 3x9=27. Only 39 fails the digit-product=12 rule, so it is the odd one out.

explanation_sections.punchline: The property to test is the product of digits, not their sum - identifying which operation unifies three numbers is the key setup decision.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: test digit sum first (34: 7, 43: 7, 62: 8, 39: 12 - not uniform), then digit product (34: 12, 43: 12, 62: 12, 39: 27 - three are uniform). Setup decision: choose the right operation (product, not sum) to identify the pattern.
explanation_sections.lesson: For digit-based odd-one-out, test both digit sum and digit product; the one that makes three values equal is the governing property.
explanation_sections.timing: 55-65 seconds. Trap: computing digit sum (which gives 7,7,8,12 - no clear pattern) and picking 62 because its sum differs from 34 and 43.
